newsitem.title: USA: Judge allows accused teenagers to do charitable work.
newsitem.headline: Judge allows accused teenagers to do charitable work.

text.p: A judge Tuesday loosened bail conditions to allow two New Jersey teenagers accused of murdering their newborn son more free time to do charitable work.
The couple, Amy Grossberg and Brian Peterson, were released from prison on $300,000 bail in January and are restricted to electronically monitored confinement in their Wyckoff, New Jersey, homes.
The high school sweethearts are charged with killing their baby Nov. 12.
Under state law, they are limited to free time in a structured setting, which previously included school or work. The judge agreed to allow to add charitable work to that category.

Grossberg and her parents and Peterson and his mother arrived together at court. During the hearing the couple sat next to each other between their attorneys, chatting occasionally and at one time holding hands.
